items.wish_description: The tremor is in {name}'s right hand now, visible whenever they hold it flat. 'One student,' they say. 'I want somebody who can close a wound properly after I have stopped being able to. Bring me the one with the patience for it, not the one with the steady hand. The steady hand goes first.'

steps.description: Gather a complete set of surgical tools from the wasteland.
{name} performs a final demonstration surgery on a willing patient.

items.completion_text: The student makes four closures on a soaked rag under the lamp while {name} watches, and says nothing at all until the third one. Then a single correction about the bite of the needle, and a nod. {name} wipes the scalpel, oils it, and puts it in the student's kit instead of back in the drawer. 'Take the rag as well,' they say. 'You will want the practice longer than you will want the knife.'

items.wish_description: Scrap steel, a length of angle iron and a cold chisel: {name} lays them out on the floor in a line, spaced, like a kit inspection. 'Every unit I served in had a wall,' they say. 'Not for the ceremony. So the count had somewhere to go. This shelter has no wall, and the shelter is the unit now.'

steps.description: Collect scrap metal and concrete for the memorial.
Recover dog tags from fallen soldiers in the wasteland.
{name} spends hours inscribing names onto the memorial wall.

items.completion_text: Eighteen names are cut into the salvaged plate, shallow and uneven, the chisel slipping twice on the last one. {name} runs a thumb along each groove to check it will hold dust and stay legible in low light, then wipes the steel down. There is no salute. 'That is everyone I can name,' they say. 'Leave the right-hand side clear. There will be more, and they should not have to go on the back.'

items.wish_description: The three oldest children are sent for, and {name} has the bedside table cleared to make room on it. 'Pulse, fever, and how to hold a hand without frightening the person in the bed,' they say. 'That is the whole of it. The other half of nursing is not going away when you are tired, and I would rather you learned this half from me than from whoever is left.'

steps.description: Find medical reference materials in the wasteland.
{name} teaches the bunker's children basic first aid and compassionate care.

items.completion_text: The children practise wraps on each other's arms until the roll runs out, and one of them does it badly enough that {name} sits up to correct the fold. That costs them, and everyone in the room notices, and nobody says so. 'Count the pulse out loud,' they say, lying back down. 'Out loud. Then you cannot lose track of where you were.'

items.wish_description: Paper, a pencil with a point on it, and privacy — {name} asks for the three in that order, and waits until the curtain is actually drawn. 'There is somebody I should have written to years ago,' they say. 'I kept not doing it because I wanted the wording to come out right. The wording was never going to come out right.'

steps.description: Find clean paper and a working pen in the wasteland.
Deliver the letter — to a living survivor, or to a grave.

items.completion_text: It takes {name} four attempts to get past the first line, and the three failures are torn into small pieces rather than left anywhere a person could read them. The finished page is short. They fold it twice, write a name and a settlement on the outside, and hand it over without asking whether it can realistically be delivered. 'If it gets there, it gets there,' they say. 'I stopped needing the answer somewhere around the second page.'

items.wish_description: What {name} wants is one specific wrench: nine-sixteenths, adjustable at the jaw, handle wrapped in strips cut from an inner tube. 'My father's, and his father's before the war,' they say. 'Second shelf of the garage at the old house, left side, behind the paint tins. If the roof has come down, look anyway. It will be under something rather than out in the weather.'

steps.description: Find the mechanic's old garage in the ruined suburbs.
Recover the heirloom wrench from the garage.

items.completion_text: The inner-tube wrap has rotted away in places and the jaw is stiff, but it is the wrench. {name} turns it over twice, finds the notch on the handle where the metal was bent once and straightened again, and stops there. 'Somebody fixed this,' they say. 'I never knew who.' They work the jaw open and shut until it moves freely, then set it on the bunk beside them instead of in the tool box.

items.wish_description: {name} wants everyone off shift at the same hour, which has not happened once since the doors closed. 'One more lesson,' they say. 'Not the curriculum — I want to teach the part I never had a period for. What you do on the morning you have decided you cannot go on, and you go on. I have notes. I would rather say it to you than leave it written down where you might not read it.'

steps.description: Help {name} prepare their final lesson materials.
Gather the bunker for {name}'s final class.

items.completion_text: It takes nineteen minutes and {name} has to sit down twice during it. Nobody leaves early and nobody talks over the end. When it is finished there is the particular silence of a room deciding what to do with its hands. Then the duty roster is read out loud, because that is the next thing, and {name} asks to hear their own name on it once more. It is there. They nod, and close the notebook.

items.wish_description: To the surface, once, in the hour before dawn — that is the whole of what {name} asks for, and they are precise about the timing. 'I want to watch it come up rather than be told about it afterwards,' they say. 'I have been describing the colour of it to people in here for a year and I am no longer certain I have the colour right.'

steps.description: Escort {name} to the surface at dawn, radiation suit and all.

items.completion_text: It comes up grey-red through the particulate, and the light arrives well before the colour does, which is not at all how {name} had been describing it. They watch the whole of it without speaking and have to be helped down off the ridge afterwards. 'I had it wrong,' they say on the walk back, and then, after a while: 'It is the same sun. I was the one who had it wrong.' They sleep through most of the following day.

items.wish_description: An analogue voltmeter, needle type, bakelite case with the lower-left corner cracked — the first tool {name} ever owned. 'My mentor gave it to me at sixteen and told me never to trust a readout I could not see move,' they say. 'It should still be on the control-room shelf at the substation, second bay, assuming the roof has held.'

steps.description: Navigate to the old electrical substation through hazardous territory.
Find and recover the voltmeter from the control room.

items.completion_text: Fed from a live circuit the needle still swings true, comes up slowly, and settles without overshoot, which is the only test that ever mattered. {name} checks the zero adjust, finds it a quarter of a scale out, and corrects it with a fingernail. Then they mount it on the wall above the distribution board, high enough to be read from the floor. 'So the next one knows where it came from,' they say. 'And so somebody notices if it ever stops being true.'

items.wish_description: {name} cleans the residue from the scale pan with a dried thumb. 'If you crush the pellets unevenly, half the dose binds to the filler,' they say. 'Watch the mortar. Once more.'

steps.description: Weigh the binding powder against the reference weight on the brass pan.
{name} guides a survivor's hands as they grind and divide five uniform powders.

items.completion_text: The powders lie in neat parchment folds, equal to the milligram. {name} sets the horn spoon in the jar and closes the drawer. 'They'll do,' they say. 'Don't let them crowd the scale.'

items.wish_description: {name} leans against the cold pipe manifold, listening with an ear pressed to the flange. 'Solder holds pressure, but vibration loosens the sleeves,' they say. 'Someone has to know which valve creeps first.'

steps.description: Inspect the drainage network joints and tighten the support saddles.
{name} marks the shutoff order on the bulkhead with red grease pencil.

items.completion_text: The red grease marks stand out on the rusted steel. The apprentice repeats the five-valve sequence without hesitating. {name} taps the header pipe once. 'It won't flood on your shift,' they say.

items.wish_description: {name} pulls a loop of rusted wire taut between two scarred fingers. 'A rabbit runs low when the crust freezes,' they say. 'Hang the noose two fingers above the snow, not four. Come here.'

steps.description: Form and notch three hair-trigger pegs using salvaged wire.
Walk the drainage perimeter with {name} and place the triggers along natural runways.

items.completion_text: The wire snare blends into the scrub brush, trembling slightly in the draught. {name} nods once. 'You watched the ground,' they say. 'Now leave it alone until dawn.'

items.wish_description: {name} unbuttons their oilcloth breast pocket and slides out a folded manifest. 'I carried this out of Fort Karkov when the gates went down,' they say. 'It belongs at Cape Beacon. Finish the route.'

steps.description: Take the sealed route manifest and verify the destination stamp.
Carry the document across the wasteland to the outpost at Cape Beacon.

items.completion_text: The station master at Cape Beacon breaks the seal, checks the route number, and signs the dispatch ledger without looking up. {name}'s route is officially closed.

items.wish_description: {name} flattens an envelope typed on scrap paper against their lap. 'Mara needs to read what actually happened to the water convoy,' they say. 'No rumors. Just the cargo numbers.'

steps.description: Accept the typed dispatch containing the verified convoy casualty record.
Hand the sealed statement directly to Mara Veln.

items.completion_text: Mara reads the single page twice, folds it into four squares, and slips it into her ledger. 'I know whose handwriting this is,' she says quietly. 'Tell them the record is straight.'

items.wish_description: {name} traces the creased edge of a notebook page written in ink long dry. 'I buried twelve people in the ash dunes before my eyes went dark,' they say. 'Lay this under the cairn marker.'

steps.description: Take the folded collect containing twelve names written in pencil.
Place the paper beneath the central stone marker at the Ash Dune Cemetery.

items.completion_text: The paper is wedged deep beneath the grey ballast stones where the salt wind cannot lift it. Back in the bunker, {name} breathes out a long, quiet sigh. 'That is the last of them,' they say.

items.wish_description: {name} stares toward the bulkhead door without blinking. 'I haven't smelled open water in nine years,' they say. 'Just grease and wet rust. Take me where the tide still breaks.'

steps.description: Escort {name} on an expedition toward the windswept shore at Cape Beacon.
Stand beside {name} at the headland as the slate-grey swell washes over the rocks.

items.completion_text: The sea wind carries a sharp tang of iodine and salt. {name} pulls their coat collar tight, watches three waves crash against the concrete breakwater, and turns back toward the track. 'All right,' they say. 'That's enough.'

items.wish_description: {name} rubs soil from under their fingernails. 'Before the sirens, I kept eight heirloom pear saplings on the terrace,' they say. 'I want to see what came up through the stone.'

steps.description: Accompany {name} to the ruined terrace pumphouse outside the perimeter.
Examine the scrub brush rooted in the cracked foundation.

items.completion_text: A twisted bramble has split the terrace flagstone, leaves yellowed by frost but alive. {name} snaps a dry twig, sniffs the pulp, and puts it in their pocket. 'It took root,' they whisper. 'The ground didn't quit.'

items.wish_description: {name} sits with elbows on knees, looking across the hall at the watchman's post. 'Marek still thinks I took his rifle sling when they locked the block,' they say. 'Tell him to come over here.'

steps.description: Bring Marek Voln to {name}'s bunk for a quiet conversation.
Sit in silence as the two men exchange short, bitter memories and finally clear the ledger.

items.completion_text: Marek stands up, wipes his palm on his coat, and clasps {name}'s shoulder for a split second before stepping away. {name} leans back against the rough wall. 'That's done,' they say. 'No debts left.'

items.wish_description: {name} stares down at their scarred palms. 'When I ran from the cult at the switchback, I left Ilze behind in the storm,' they say. 'I need her to know I didn't point them to her trail.'

steps.description: Arrange a private moment with Dr. Ilze Kaar during her morning rounds.
Let {name} tell Dr. Kaar the true sequence of Day 14 at the switchback shrine.

items.completion_text: Dr. Kaar listens without interrupting, then sets down her clipboard and takes {name}'s pulse. 'I found my own way out,' she says evenly. 'You don't carry that anymore.' {name} closes their eyes.

items.wish_description: {name} gestures toward the crowded infirmary corridor with a tired nod. 'I've wrapped eighty-four bodies in this trench,' they say. 'I don't want someone elbowing my cot to reach a drip stand. Give me a quiet corner.'

steps.description: Clear and drape a secluded alcove in the lower storage corridor away from the wards.
Prepare a cot with clean canvas and sit vigil while the corridor quietens.

items.completion_text: The storage alcove is dim and cool, smelling only of damp masonry and clean canvas. {name} lies back with their hands resting on their chest. 'Good,' they say softly. 'A proper room.'

items.wish_description: {name} draws a small, dry pouch from their tunic. 'No needles and no shouting,' they whisper. 'Just steep the bitter herb on the burner and sit with me while the lamp burns out.'

steps.description: Boil a pot of water with dried herbs on the shelter stove.
Sit beside {name}'s cot in silence as the herbal steam clears the heavy air.

items.completion_text: The sharp, bitter scent of thyme and sage drifts through the partition. {name}'s breathing slows to a peaceful rhythm in the warm stillness. 'Thank you,' they murmur. 'Peace upon this house.'

items.wish_description: {name} cleans their small screwdrivers one by one on oiled cloth. 'I don't need speeches or a gathering,' they say. 'Just let me set my bench in order before my fingers stiffen.'

steps.description: Help {name} arrange tweezers, loupes, and movement trays in numerical order.
Watch {name} give the brass pendulum clock its weekly forty turns.

items.completion_text: The brass escapement ticks with a steady, hollow resonance against the bulkhead. {name} places the key in the centre of the felt pad. 'Seven days of accurate time,' they say. 'Keep it wound.'

items.wish_description: {name} swallows hard, their throat dry from fever. 'Ration paste tastes like tin,' they say. 'Boil two tubers with coarse salt until the water turns sweet. Just like the kitchen in winter.'

steps.description: Bring fresh tubers and preservation salt to the galley stove.
Simmer the roots slowly until tender and bring a hot bowl to {name}.

items.completion_text: {name} spoons the clear, salty broth slowly, savoring every swallow. A faint trace of color touches their cheeks. 'The steam smells like home,' they whisper. 'The real kitchen.'

items.wish_description: {name} sits on their bunk holding an empty tin cup. 'I haven't shared a hot breakfast with the children since the power failed,' they say. 'Heat a tin of beans with water so they can eat first.'

steps.description: Heat preserved rations and clean water over the galley burner.
Sit with {name} as their child eats from the warm cup before dawn.

items.completion_text: The child scrapes the bottom of the tin clean and smiles. {name} rests a heavy hand on the boy's hair, breathing shallowly. 'They're fed,' they say. 'They have what they need.'

items.wish_description: {name} pulls you down close by the collar. 'Under the ventilation trunk on Sub-Level 2,' they wheeze. 'Three tins of meat and two rolls of bandage. I stole them during the rationing panic.'

steps.description: Write down the exact coordinates of the hidden sub-floor cache.
Retrieve the hidden stores from beneath the ventilation duct.

items.completion_text: The recovered tins and bandages are logged back into the common store. {name} lets go of your sleeve and exhales a ragged breath. 'Put it on the open shelves,' they say. 'It was never mine.'

items.wish_description: {name} looks up with hollow, sleepless eyes. 'On Day 3, when the blast alarm sounded, I gave the order to seal Outer Hatch C,' they say. 'There were forty people on the ramp. Write it down.'

steps.description: Transcribe {name}'s unvarnished account of the Outer Hatch C lockout order.
File the signed statement into the official bunker archive.

items.completion_text: The ledger page is stamped and placed into the permanent casualty files. {name} stares at their hands, unclenched for the first time in years. 'They deserve to have it written true,' they say.

items.wish_description: {name} grips your wrist with surprising strength. 'My girl cannot stand the dark alone,' they whisper. 'Promise me Lina gets a place near the heater, and that someone walks her to the washroom.'

steps.description: Speak with Lina and establish a formal guardianship assignment in the roster.
Reassign Lina's sleeping space to the warm alcove beside the duty station.

items.completion_text: Lina's bedding is laid out in the warm nook near the central stove. {name} watches from across the room, her grip finally softening. 'She will be warm,' she whispers. 'Thank you.'

items.wish_description: {name} glances toward Niko, who is shivering in the corridor corner. 'Niko does whatever anyone asks of him until he drops,' they say. 'Make sure someone checks his rations every day.'

steps.description: Assure Niko that his daily allocation and work shifts are protected.
Log a permanent note in the duty roster ensuring Niko's rest shifts are enforced.

items.completion_text: Niko holds his ration card with both hands, nodding timidly. {name} rests their head back against the pillow. 'He was always too quiet to ask,' they say. 'Watch over him.'

items.wish_description: {name} reaches deep under their mattress and pulls out a silver medal wrapped in felt. 'I took this off an altar at Switchback Waystation,' they mutter. 'It belongs on the memorial. Take it back.'

steps.description: Accept the tarnished silver medal and check the inscribed regimental number.
Travel to Switchback Waystation and place the medal back upon the shrine altar.

items.completion_text: The silver medal rests once more in the weathered stone niche above the mountain track. Back in the shelter, {name} breathes easier. 'I carried that curse four hundred miles,' they say. 'It's home.'

items.wish_description: {name} opens a small tin box containing personal military identification tags. 'These belonged to the surveyor who mapped the aquifer before the bombs,' they say. 'Hang them on the Memorial Wall.'

steps.description: Inspect the embossed serial number on the personal dog tags.
Inscribe the surveyor's name into the memorial ledger and hang the tags on the steel wall.

items.completion_text: The dog tags click softly against the steel wall before hanging still. {name} traces the embossed letters one last time. 'Names outlast governments,' they whisper. 'Remember him.'

items.wish_description: {name} places a ring of heavy brass keys on top of the quarterly inventory ledger. 'The supply room cannot have two masters,' they say. 'Call Oskar in. He knows how to count without stealing.'

steps.description: Bring Oskar Ruut to the quartermaster's desk to receive the inventory balance.
Formally hand over the supply room keys and the signed handover ledger.

items.completion_text: Oskar takes the heavy key ring, testing the weight in his hand, and signs his initials beside {name}'s last entry. {name} nods, their duty discharged. 'Count it twice on Tuesdays,' they say.

items.wish_description: {name} keeps a folded note in their coat. 'I wrote it to a girl who bought from my counter,' they say. 'Before. I turned her away the day the sirens went. I want her to know I'm sorry.' Whether she lived, {name} doesn't know.

steps.description: Search the bunker's records for any sign of the woman {name} turned away.
{name} reads the note aloud to the bunker's hearth, in case she is listening somewhere.

items.completion_text: {name} reads the apology to an empty room and a cold stove. No one answers. {name} folds the note back into their coat and closes their eyes. 'That's all I owed her,' they say. 'The rest was never mine to fix.'

items.wish_description: {name} asks after a survivor who stopped speaking to them months ago. 'I told them their grief was a kind of faith,' they say quietly. 'They needed me to sit with it, not name it. I'd like to sit with them now.'

steps.description: Locate the survivor who withdrew from {name}.
Sit with them for an hour, saying nothing unless they speak first.

items.completion_text: {name} sits beside the other survivor until the lamp burns low. Neither of them says much. When {name} finally rises, the other nods once — small, but real. 'Thank you for staying,' they murmur. 'Thank you for not explaining.'

items.wish_description: {name} remembers a student they failed. 'I told him he'd amount to nothing,' they say. 'He was sixteen. He didn't need my verdict — he needed my patience. If he's still out there, I'd take the words back.'

steps.description: Ask whether the former student survived, or where they were last seen.
{name} writes down, in plain words, that they were wrong.

items.completion_text: {name} pins the retraction to the bunker wall where anyone passing might read it. 'I was a fool with a chalkboard,' it ends. 'Whoever you became, you deserved better than my verdict.' {name} looks tired, but lighter. 'Words don't travel back,' they say. 'But they can travel forward.'

items.wish_description: {name} can't stop thinking about a dog they couldn't save — a neighbor's, before the move to the bunker. 'The owners are gone now, almost certainly. But the dog might still be at the house. Waiting. I owe it a look.'

steps.description: Locate the neighbor's house in the ruined suburbs.
If the dog is gone, bring back its collar for the owners' memory.

items.completion_text: The house is empty, the bowl dry and cracked. {name} picks up the collar from the floor, brushing the dust off the tag. They carry it back without a word. 'I couldn't save it,' they say. 'But I can remember whose it was. That's the least of the work I do.'

items.wish_description: {name} speaks carefully about a daughter who left home years before the bombs. 'She hated the trade,' they say. 'Said I made my living off the dead. She wasn't wrong. I'd like to know she made it underground somewhere — anyone's underground.'

steps.description: Send word with the next caravan: has anyone sheltered a woman of that name?
{name} leaves a recorded message where travelers might find it.

items.completion_text: No answer comes back — not yet, maybe never. {name} records the message anyway, voice steady despite everything. 'I'm proud of what you built away from me,' it says. 'You were right to go.' They set down the recorder. 'Even if she never hears it,' they say, 'the air heard it. That has to count for something.'

items.wish_description: {name} laughs, then stops. 'There was a cook. Better than me, honestly. We sabotaged each other for years — stealing recipes, bad-mouthing the other's stock. Stupid. I'd cook him one meal, no tricks, if he were here.'

steps.description: Get an improvised cooking stove lit and steady.
{name} prepares the dish the way the rival would have made it — his way, not theirs.

items.completion_text: {name} plates the meal for no one and sets it on the counter. 'His way,' they say. 'Browned longer, salted less. He was right about that.' They leave it to cool. The bunker eats well that night, and no one asks why {name} is quiet. 'A rival's just a friend you were too proud to lose,' they say.

items.wish_description: {name} confesses something old. 'I reported a colleague. He was drinking before operations. I was right to. But I did it to hurt him, not to save his patients — and I've known the difference ever since. I'd like to say it plain, before I can't.'

steps.description: Find someone in the bunker willing to hear a confession without judging.
{name} states, aloud and without excuse, what they did and why.

items.completion_text: {name} finishes speaking. The listener says nothing for a long moment, then: 'You were right about the surgery. You were wrong about yourself. Both can be true.' {name} exhales slowly. 'That's the first honest verdict I've had,' they say. 'Thank you for not softening it.'

items.wish_description: {name} and their brother hadn't spoken in a decade over an inheritance that no longer exists. 'A workshop,' {name} says. 'We fought over a workshop that's slag now. If he's alive, I'd hand him the whole thing. Twice over.'

steps.description: Check the bunker's intake lists and caravan records for {name}'s brother.
Whether or not he's found, {name} writes the workshop over to him in plain terms.

items.completion_text: {name} scratches out a deed on scrap paper — to a building that is glass and ash. 'It's his,' they say. 'Always should have been.' They fold it small and tuck it away. 'If he comes looking, he'll find it. If he doesn't, the record stands anyway. Either way I stop carrying it.'

items.wish_description: {name} remembers a source they named in print to save their own career. 'She disappeared after that. I told myself she'd have been found out anyway. I don't believe it anymore. I'd like to find her, or her family, and own it.'

steps.description: Follow what leads remain to find the source or any kin.
{name} writes the true version and reads it aloud, naming themselves as the one at fault.

items.completion_text: {name} reads the retraction to the bunker, voice flat. 'I named her to save myself,' it says. 'That was the story. The rest was excuse.' No one interrupts. When it's done, {name} sets the page down. 'Print will outlast me,' they say. 'Let it outlast me with the truth in it.'

items.wish_description: {name} carries a name they never thanked. 'A man pulled me out of a building, decades back. Never said a word after. I was too proud to thank him. I'd like to find his grave, if there is one, and stand there a minute.'

steps.description: Locate where the old comrade is buried, or was last seen.
Stand at the place and say the thanks {name} never gave.

items.completion_text: {name} stands a long while at the marker — or at the empty ground where a marker ought to be. 'Thank you,' they say, simply. 'You didn't have to. You did.' They walk back slowly. 'Took me forty years and the end of the world to say three words,' they murmur. 'But I said them.'

items.wish_description: {name} left their dispensary ledger behind. 'Not for the dosages,' they say. 'The names. Everyone I ever sold to. I'd like to know who I knew. If someone could fetch it...'

steps.description: Find the old pharmacy where {name} worked.
Recover the dispensary ledger from behind the counter.

items.completion_text: {name} turns the pages slowly, reading names aloud, one by one. Some they pause on. Some they pass quickly. At the end they close the book and hold it against their chest. 'I knew all these people,' they say. 'Most of them are gone now. But I knew them. That book is proof.'

items.wish_description: {name} kept the first collar they ever fitted — a stray they treated for free, years ago. 'It's in a tin at the clinic. I'd like to hold it. It reminds me I started this work because I liked animals, not because I was good at it.'

steps.description: Find the old veterinary clinic in the ruins.
Recover the tin with the collar from the back room.

items.completion_text: {name} turns the worn leather collar over in their hands. The buckle is green with age. 'She bit me the whole time I fitted it,' they say, almost smiling. 'I deserved it. I was clumsy.' They set it on their chest. 'Start with liking them,' they say. 'The skill comes, or it doesn't. The liking is the part that mattered.'

items.wish_description: {name} kept a register of every person they laid to rest. 'It's in the chapel vestry,' they say. 'Names, dates, a line each. I'd like it brought here. People deserve to be remembered, even if I'm the only one who'll read the book.'

steps.description: Locate the old chapel vestry where {name} kept the register.
Carry the burial register back to the bunker.

items.completion_text: {name} sets the heavy book on the table and opens it to the first page. They read a name aloud, and a date, and the single line they wrote. Then the next. The bunker goes quiet, listening. 'These are people,' {name} says. 'Each one. I won't let the count swallow them.'

items.wish_description: {name} learned to solder with their grandfather's iron — heavy, brass, stained black at the tip. 'It's in the workshop at the old house. I taught three people to splice wire with that iron. I'd like to teach a fourth before I go.'

steps.description: Find {name}'s grandfather's workshop.
Recover the soldering iron from the bench.

items.completion_text: {name} plugs the iron in and it still heats. They call over a younger survivor and show them, slowly, how to tin the tip. 'Like this,' they say. 'Patience, then heat, then the join. In that order.' The young one's first splice holds. {name} nods, satisfied. 'That iron's taught four of us now,' they say. 'It'll teach more.'

items.wish_description: {name} once did a story on the astronomers at the observatory. 'They told me the stars would outlast everything we'd built,' they say. 'I'd like to go up there one more time. See if they were right. See if the stars are still there, and what I built is not.'

steps.description: Escort {name} to the silent observatory at nightfall.
Open the dome and let {name} look through the old eyepiece.

items.completion_text: The dome groans open on rusted tracks. Above the ash, the stars are there — dimmer, but there. {name} looks for a long time. 'They were right,' they whisper. 'The stars are still there. Everything I chased is not. And somehow that's a comfort, not a grief.' They close the dome gently. 'Let the sky keep its peace.'

items.wish_description: {name} wants to go back to the gymnasium where they first taught. 'Not for the lessons,' they say. 'For the echo. A gymnasium has a particular echo when it's full of children. I want to know if it still echoes, even empty.'

steps.description: Bring {name} to the old school gymnasium.
{name} stands at center court and speaks, listening to the room answer.

items.completion_text: {name} stands at half-court and calls roll — names from twenty years back. The gymnasium gives each one back, hollow and stretched. When the last name fades, {name} is quiet a long while. 'It still echoes,' they say, smiling thin. 'Empty rooms remember better than full ones, I think. The sound has nowhere to hide.'

items.wish_description: {name} wants to stand on Bridge Seven one last time. 'I crossed it the day I came home,' they say. 'It was the moment the war was over for me. I'd like to stand on it again, now that there's a new war. See if the river still runs underneath.'

steps.description: Escort {name} to Bridge Seven.
{name} stands at the railing and watches the water below.

items.completion_text: The bridge is buckled but standing. Below, the river still moves — muddy, slow, alive. {name} grips the railing and breathes. 'I came home over this bridge once,' they say. 'I'm not coming home this time. But the river didn't stop. I take some comfort in that.' They turn to leave. 'The water doesn't know about wars,' they say. 'Good for it.'

items.wish_description: {name} buried people in the collapsed salt mine when the ground above was too hot. 'I'd like to go back,' they say. 'Not to dig. Just to sit at the mouth and let them know someone came. They were alone when I left them there. I hated that part.'

steps.description: Escort {name} to the collapsed salt mine entrance.
{name} sits at the entrance and speaks the names of those buried inside.

items.completion_text: {name} sits a long time at the dark mouth of the mine, naming the dead into the shaft. The wind takes the names and gives nothing back. 'I know you can't hear me,' they say finally. 'But I came anyway. You weren't alone when it mattered — I was there. And I'm here now.' They rise stiffly. 'That's the work. Showing up. The rest is just carpentry.'

items.wish_description: {name} has a different sort of wish. 'There's a ledger. Not the dispensary one — another. Things I did for money, after hours. If anyone reads it, three families break. I want it burned. Let what I did die with me.'

steps.description: Recover {name}'s private ledger from its hiding place.
Burn the ledger unopened, in front of a witness.

items.completion_text: {name} feeds the ledger to the flame page by page, never reading a line. The witness watches the last corner curl to ash. 'Some debts die with the debtor,' {name} says. 'That's not mercy — it's judgment. I'm choosing who carries this, and it stops with me.' The ash scatters. 'Let them remember me kind,' they say. 'It's a lie I've earned.'

items.wish_description: {name} has a confession they refuse to make. 'I buried a man who wasn't dead,' they say, voice level. 'He'd wronged someone I loved. I buried him conscious. I've kept it thirty years. I won't confess it now and make it someone else's burden. It goes into the ground with me.'

steps.description: {name} writes the secret down, once, on a single page — not to share, but to face.
{name} destroys the page unread by anyone else.

items.completion_text: {name} writes the truth on one page, reads it to themselves, and burns it. The witness sees only the flame. 'I faced it,' {name} says. 'That's between me and it now. Not you, not the bunker, not whatever comes after. Some debts are carried to the grave, and that is where they belong.' They close their eyes. 'Let me be the only one who loses sleep over it.'

items.wish_description: {name} surprises everyone. 'There's a man who asks my forgiveness every time he sees me,' they say. 'I've withheld it, because he hasn't earned it and I won't cheapen it. I want to die still withholding it. Forgiveness isn't a door you kick down on your way out. It's a gift. He can live without it. I have.'

steps.description: {name} states plainly what was done, and why it remains unforgiven.
{name} refuses, one final time, to grant the forgiveness requested.

items.completion_text: {name} speaks the unforgiven thing aloud, names its weight, and declines to absolve it. 'I forgive much,' they say. 'I've built a life on it. But not this. Not him. To forgive what hasn't been reckoned with would be to lie, and I've given my life to not lying about this.' They fold their hands. 'Let him live with it. I have. And now I'll die with it, intact. That's mine.'

items.wish_description: {name} has a cassette — a recording of a friend confessing to something that would exile him from the bunker. 'I kept it as insurance,' {name} says. 'I'm ashamed I kept it. He's dead now. I want it destroyed, so no one ever hears it and judges him. His ledger's closed.'

steps.description: Recover the hidden cassette from {name}'s stash.
Destroy the cassette unplayed, in front of a witness.

items.completion_text: {name} sets the cassette on the floor and brings a wrench down on it. The tape spools crack and spill. The witness sees only the wreckage. 'He was more than his worst day,' {name} says. 'I kept this as a weapon. That was wrong. Now it's nothing, and so is my hold over him.' They sweep the pieces into the bin. 'Let his name stay clean. He earned that much from me.'
